subject: Private deployment SKU tiers, platform fee structure & support credit request
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-health.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acme-health.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SKU tiers, platform fee structure & support credit request

Stephanie — thanks for the call earlier. Two asks from our side so we can move this to procurement: 1) a clear SKU table that maps committed capacity (GPUs / vCPUs), platform fee, and included support hours; 2) confirmation of whether we can take a one-time onboarding credit to offset the first 3 months of platform fees while we validate performance.

We attached the initial SOW constraints and a list of compliance docs. Can Redwood provide a simple numeric example (monthly cost) for our 4-region deployment with HA? Goal is to get an internal PO approved by 9/30.

Thanks,
Samir
VP, Infrastructure — Acme Health
[Attachment: Acme_SOW_constraints.pdf (pdf)]

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-health.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SKU tiers, platform fee structure & support credit request

Samir — appreciate the clear asks. I’m looping in Michael (pricing) and Lauren (eng ops) to confirm the SKU mapping and the onboarding credit policy. High-level: we can provide a SKU table that maps reserved GPU pool sizes to a platform fee band and 24/7 support tiers. Onboarding credits are usually dealt as a one-time service credit tied to a 12-month commit. I’ll get a worked example and a spreadsheet by EOD Friday.

Quick clarifying Qs for the example you mentioned:
- Expected sustained concurrency (tokens/s) or QPS for the four regions?
- Any hard requirements on cold-start P50 latency?
- Do you want HA across regions (active/active) or active/passive fallback?

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: request_acknowledged.txt (txt)]

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-health.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment SKU tiers, platform fee structure & support credit request

Samir / Stephanie — attaching the SKU matrix and two worked examples: (A) minimal three-pool deployment (US West + US East) with active/passive failover, (B) full four-region active/active. In both we show: reserved GPU count, platform fee tier, included support hours (business vs 24/7), and incremental per-token uplift for burst capacity.

Onboarding credit: we can offer a time-bound one-time platform-fee credit equal to ~50% of month 1–3 platform fees, conditioned on a 12mo reserved commitment and signed SOW. If procurement needs different structuring (e.g., spread vs upfront credit), we can do a credit schedule tied to milestones (PO in, acceptance test complete).

Notes on exclusions: quantization and custom kernel work are out-of-scope of the onboarding credit unless explicitly scoped in SOW.

Files: Redwood_Private_SKU_matrix_v3.xlsx (attached)

—Michael
Principal Pricing Manager — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Private_SKU_matrix_v3.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acme-health.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SKU tiers, platform fee structure & support credit request

Thanks Michael — the matrix is helpful. A few procurement-scope items and redlines from our counsel attached. Main asks: 1) Can the onboarding credit be recognized as an invoice credit (spread over Q1) rather than a lump sum? 2) We need a Support SLA addendum that clarifies response and resolution SLAs for on-prem incidents and a defined escalation path for security incidents. 3) We need a firm expiry on the pricing table (we ask 45 days).

If those are workable we can circulate a PO the week of 9/27.

Emily Zhao
Sr. Manager, Procurement — Acme Health
[Attachment: Acme_Redlines_20260920.pdf (pdf)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acme-health.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme-health.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SKU tiers, platform fee structure & support credit request

Emily — thanks for the redlines. Quick responses below and next steps so procurement has a clean path to PO: 

1) Onboarding credit recognition: we can do an invoice credit schedule that amortizes the credit over the first 3 invoices (Q1) so it appears as a credit line item rather than a single negative invoice. Finance will include required language in the SOW.

2) Support SLA addendum: Lauren will send a draft SLA addendum within 24 hours that captures 4hr P1 response / 8hr P1 remediation target for private on-prem incidents and an explicit security escalation chain (Security Ops -> CISO on-call). This will be appended to the SOW and subject to final legal review.

3) Pricing expiry: we can hold the quoted SKU matrix for 45 days from 2026-09-21. I’ll mark the spreadsheet and the DocuSign envelope accordingly.

Next steps: Lauren to share SLA addendum; Michael to stamp the SKU matrix with expiry and include the amortized credit schedule; I’ll prepare a short email to confirm the PO acceptance checklist for Acme procurement. If all looks good, target PO week of 9/27.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: PO_checklist_template.txt (txt)]
